title: Auto-land a passing run (per-project opt-in)
lead: *Proposed.* Drafted 2026-11-11. Size M. In the v1.1 relay the owner's standing rule was "land any slice whose gate returns `VERDICT: PASS` without asking". The orchestrator applied it by hand on every run: read `gate-N.md`, mark human checks "later", run `ork approve`, then push. This slice lets a project opt in to ork doing that step itself, within limits the owner sets. Push already exists (`ork projects set P --push on`, `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:311`).
findings_note: Every v1.1 landing was a hand approve after VERDICT: PASS under the owner's standing rule.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
*Proposed.* Evidence:

- Owner, 2026-11-07: "land any passing slice without asking approval" (memory `landing-needs-no-approval`), and "Push after every landing". Every landing on 2026-11-08 to 11-11 followed the same hand steps: confirm `VERDICT: PASS` with `ork show RUN gate-N.md`, run `ork check RUN N later` for each human check, run any orchestrator-only Check lines (adj 263), then `ork approve RUN` and `git push origin main`.
- Adj 162 (`landing.in-ork`): ork lands after the owner approves. Auto-land changes who approves, so it needs a new adj record from the owner. It does not edit 162.

Open owner questions (the owner answers before the relay starts; key `landing.auto-approve`):
- Q1 whether to do this at all, and its default. (a) a per-project setting `ork projects set P --auto-land on|off`, off by default (recommended). (b) a per-run flag `ork run ... --auto-land`. (c) do not build it; the approve step stays by hand.
- Q2 human checks. (a) a run with human checks is auto-landed with each check marked "later", and the landed list shows them (recommended: it matches the hand practice in this relay). (b) any human check blocks auto-land.
- Q3 orchestrator-only Check lines (adj 263). (a) a run whose spec has any Check line not run by ork's checks is never auto-landed; it waits for `ork approve` (recommended). (b) auto-land anyway.
- Q4 which gate results count. (a) only `VERDICT: PASS` with no `[owner]` finding left open and the full check green (recommended). (b) as (a), plus a notice before landing.

sections.body:
- `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:311-425` (`projects set`: the setting)
- `internal/registry` (the project field)

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- Engine: a run with gate PASS, no owner finding and green checks lands with no approve call; its human checks end as `later` and appear in `human-checks-todo.md` in the landing commit.
- Engine: a gate FAIL, an open `[owner]` finding, or a red check leaves the run in awaiting-approval or its existing pause; nothing is appended.
- Engine: a project with `auto_land` off waits for `ork approve` as today.
- Registry and CLI: `ork projects set P --auto-land off` stores `auto_land: false`; an absent field reads as on; `--auto-land maybe` is a usage error.
- Todo file: a missing file is created with the header; an existing file gets one new section appended and keeps its other text byte for byte.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Read how a run reaches awaiting-approval and how `ork approve` lands it (`internal/engine/approval.go`, the daemon approve handler). Record the entry points in the slice notes.
2. Add the per-project field `auto_land` to the registry (absent means on), and `ork projects set P --auto-land on|off` (adj 281: default on for every project; off is only an opt-out).
3. When a run would enter awaiting-approval with gate `VERDICT: PASS`, no open `[owner]` finding and green checks, and the project has not opted out, the engine runs the same path as an approve call: mark each human check `later`, then land and clean up. Any other case waits for `ork approve` as today, with its existing reason.
4. At landing, append the run's human checks to `human-checks-todo.md` at the project root (create it with the header used in this repo when it is missing), under `## ID (run RUN, DATE)` as `- [ ] TEXT` lines, with a leading `deferred to land:` replaced by `[AFTER LAND]`. Commit it with the landing's tracking commit, by path.
5. A landing pause (merge conflict, failed land checks) behaves as today; `ork retry` continues the automatic landing.
6. Docs (*proposed*): design.md (approval and landing), guide.md (no approve step; the todo file), dashboard.md if the approval card text changes.
7. CHANGELOG.md: one bullet under `## Unreleased` (*proposed*).
